clue.text: Spar has bread in front of till

indicators.note: says the bread word comes before the spar word in the entry

parts.note: bread is slang for money
to spar is to box, as boxers do in training

explanation.surface: A supermarket chain (Spar) has its bread displayed beside the checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar looks like the convenience-store chain; here it is the verb meaning to box. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is a container for cash, as is a savings box with a slot.

clue.text: Cut each last weed in field

indicators.note: the word for cut goes around the other pieces, which sit in it

parts.note: to cut grass is to mow it

indicators.note: the final letter of the word weed is the one taken

explanation.surface: A gardener mows every last weed growing in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an action on the weed; it supplies the outer piece, with 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often cut for hay.

clue.text: Move scenery as required

indicators.note: moving the letters of these two words rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A stagehand's instruction: shift the scenery as needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges SCENERY AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required is needed or essential, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Always rejected Twitter's right wing points and threads

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for always
the right wing, or rightmost edge, of the word Twitter is its final letter R
N and S are compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: Political talk: right-wingers on Twitter keep getting their points and threads rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AY into YA; the right-hand end of the word Twitter (ignoring the 's) gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarns are spun threads, as used in knitting and weaving.

clue.text: Huge al fresco day out includes heading to zoo

indicators.note: the abbreviation for day is taken out of the word for al fresco
the word for al fresco then takes in a new letter in that same spot

parts.note: al fresco means in the open air, outside

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word zoo is the one used

explanation.surface: An enormous outdoor day out that takes in a visit to the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: In OUTSIDE, 'out' removes D and 'includes' puts in Z, the 'heading to' zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsize describes something unusually large, especially clothing sizes, so it equals huge.

clue.text: Still shortly intend to join police

indicators.note: said briefly, so the word for intend loses its last letter

parts.note: to intend something is to plan it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: Someone intends to join the police force before long but hasn't yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb ('yet'); it is the adjective for calm. 'shortly' trims PLAN to PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water or a still mood is calm and undisturbed, which is what placid means.

clue.text: Seem keen to get a move on

parts.note: to seem a certain way is to look it
keen, as in a blade or a mind, means sharp

explanation.surface: Trying to appear eager in order to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'look sharp' is an order to hurry, just as 'get a move on' is.

clue.text: Rise of Conservative member

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: The advancement of a Tory member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like an MP; it is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go up, as one does on a ladder or a hill: a synonym.

clue.text: Comic verse cruelly eviscerated Lloyd George

indicators.note: treated cruelly, the letters are knocked into a new arrangement
with its insides removed, only the outer letters of Lloyd remain

explanation.surface: A satirical poem savaged the former prime minister David Lloyd George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eviscerated' leaves LD from Lloyd; 'cruelly' rearranges LD plus GEORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is crude, comic or badly made verse.

clue.text: In gold, carats' value is precise

indicators.note: the carat letters go in the gold symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
c is an abbreviation for carat, doubled here for the plural
to rate something is to value it

explanation.surface: A jeweller's claim that a gold item's carat value is exact.
explanation.walkthrough: Carat abbreviates to c, and doubling a letter for a plural follows the pp-for-pages convention. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and precise are synonyms: both mean exactly correct.

clue.text: Judge old man playing the fool

parts.note: a man is a chess piece, and the king is one

explanation.surface: A judge describes an old man as clowning around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone joking is fooling around, not being serious.

clue.text: State of West Virginia raised ordinary income

indicators.note: read as in-come, it says the letter comes into the other piece
in a down entry, raised means written upwards, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A query about the state of household incomes in West Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like the US state; it is the verb meaning declare. 'raised' turns W VA into AVW and O comes in: 'income' read as 'in come'.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow something is to declare it openly, to state it.

clue.text: Gets rid of letters penned by infamous Tsar

indicators.note: the run of letters is held within the words that follow, as if written by them

explanation.surface: A notorious Russian ruler disposes of correspondence he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove or expel them: a synonym of getting rid of.

clue.text: Perhaps sister's wearing veil in order not to be seen

indicators.note: the sibling is dressed in the other letters, which go around it
putting these letters in order rearranges them

parts.note: a sister is an example of a sib, or sibling; 'Perhaps' signals the example

explanation.surface: A sister puts on a veil so that she cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like 'so as to'; 'in' is fodder and 'order' alone signals the rearrangement, whose letters split around the sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invisible cannot be seen, so the phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Deer taken by lion's making a comeback challenge

indicators.note: coming back means running backwards, so the joined letters are reversed
the deer word is followed by the lion word before they turn around

parts.note: an elk is a kind of deer
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A deer caught by a lion; the lion stages a return challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: ELK CAT is reversed by 'making a comeback'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a problem or opponent is to take it on, to challenge it.

clue.text: Look up article supporting federal leader — it's hard to stay loyal

indicators.note: in a down entry the article sits beneath, holding up the federal letter
in a down entry, up means written from the bottom, so the look word runs backwards

parts.note: to peek is to look

indicators.note: the leader of the word federal is its first letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the word it, with 's as a link
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Studying a federal leader's record shows how hard it is to remain loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEEK into KEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep faith with someone is an idiom for remaining loyal to them.

clue.text: Wife takes right approach in quarrel

parts.note: an angle is an approach or point of view

explanation.surface: A wife takes the correct line in a domestic argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrangle is a long noisy dispute, so it is a quarrel.

clue.text: Have lunch in garden relaxed with large dog

indicators.note: the eating word goes into the rearranged letters
relaxed means loosened, so the letters of garden are rearranged

parts.note: to have lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: Lunch in the garden, relaxing with a big dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' rearranges the garden letters, and the lunch word sits in them after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a breed of very large dog, so this is an example.

clue.text: Love writer's intellect and unprejudiced way of thinking

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a pen is a writer, with 's as a link
mind means intellect

explanation.surface: An author's love and intelligence make for a broad-minded outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author; it is the tool, a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An open mind is a receptive, unbiased attitude: an idiom for thinking without prejudice.

clue.text: May freak when imprisoned without charge

indicators.note: without means outside, so the imprisoned word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in

indicators.note: to freak out is to go wild, so the letters of May are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone named May panics when locked up without being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' reads as 'not accused'; 'without' means outside here, and 'charge' is the definition. 'freak' makes AYM.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a fee or price asked, the sum paid for something.

clue.text: In Marseilles you catch endless fish

parts.note: tu is the French for you, Marseilles being in France

indicators.note: without its end, the catch word loses its final letter

parts.note: to nab is to catch

explanation.surface: A French fishing tip: in Marseilles you catch fish without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Company has power for every PC

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
per means for each, for every

explanation.surface: A firm has electrical power for every personal computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a personal computer; it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A PC, a police constable, is a police officer, slangily called a cop or copper.

clue.text: On telephone makes certain promises of money

indicators.note: heard over the phone, only the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to make certain of something is to check it

explanation.surface: Someone on the phone guarantees payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order for a bank to pay money, effectively a promise of payment.

clue.text: Father has bother with rain regularly coming in

indicators.note: these letters come into the bother word

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance, a bother

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word rain

explanation.surface: Dad is troubled by rain getting in on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes RI from rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the title of a Catholic priest.

clue.text: Ducks fine in new enclosure, hope you don't mind

indicators.note: the ducks and fine letters go in the other letters

parts.note: a fence encloses a space
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, O, so ducks are OO
f is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Healthy ducks in a newly fenced pen; a polite apology to a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OOF goes between N and FENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No offence' is said as an apology in advance: the speaker hopes the listener isn't upset.

clue.text: Generally get mushy when son leaves

indicators.note: the son letter leaves, taken out of the mushy word

parts.note: to get mushy is to soften

explanation.surface: People usually grow sentimental once their son leaves home.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, as in most cases, much like generally.

clue.text: Overt corruption in key part of democratic process

indicators.note: corruption spoils the word overt, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Blatant vote-rigging in an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters are the citizens who cast ballots, central to how democracy works.

clue.text: Praises avenue lined with elevated flower containers

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means read upwards, so the hidden run is reversed
the letters lie inside, lining the words Praises avenue

explanation.surface: Someone admires a street lined with raised flower pots.
explanation.walkthrough: SESAV hides in 'praiSES AVenue'; 'elevated' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Vases are vessels for holding cut flowers.

clue.text: Have a hunch some Latin tuition's required

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run held within them

explanation.surface: A feeling that some Latin lessons are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to know by instinct, which is having a hunch.

clue.text: Futile pursuit of cup's plucky

parts.note: a mug is a cup, here with 's
game means brave, plucky

explanation.surface: A trophy cup's chase is a brave but fruitless one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an idiom for a pointless activity only a fool would pursue.

clue.text: Row with young girl about stowing drug in boat

parts.note: a din is a row, a loud noise

indicators.note: the turned letters stow the drug letter, holding it inside
about means turned around, so these two letters run backwards

parts.note: g is a dictionary abbreviation for girl
H is slang for heroin, a drug

explanation.surface: An argument with a young girl about drugs hidden on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like rowing, apt for a boat; it is a din. 'about' turns YG to GY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, often towed or carried by a larger vessel.

clue.text: Easiest solution's one to be adopted in my opinion

indicators.note: the one letter is taken in, adopted by the rearranged letters
a solution resolves things into a new form, so the letters of easiest are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A solver's view that the simplest answer is the one to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution's' rearranges EASIEST; 'to be adopted' takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As I see it' introduces a personal view, the same idiom as in my opinion.
